precepts.text: I am very sore displeased with the heathen that are at ease: for I was but a little displeased, and they helped forward the affliction. Yes, we sinned against our God, and the Lord allowed us to go into the hands of our enemies, but they took it too far.
precepts.point: In closing: there is a time wherein one man ruleth over another to his own hurt. That is Esau. The way Esau treated us is going to be to his own detriment.

note.label: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

precepts.why:
“there is a time wherein one man ruleth over another to his own hurt.” That is Esau. The way Esau treated us is going to be to his own detriment.

The Lord says it in Zechariah: “And I am very sore displeased with the heathen that are at ease: for I was but a little displeased, and they helped forward the affliction.” Yes, we sinned against our God. Yes, the Lord allowed us to go into the hands of our enemies. But they took it too far.

God was but a little displeased with Israel, and the heathen helped forward the affliction. You think Christ ain't see that? That is why Esau's rule over Jacob is to his own hurt: he went past what God allowed, and the Lord is sore displeased with him for it.

precepts.text: And I am very sore displeased with the heathen that are at ease: for I was but a little displeased, and they helped forward the affliction. God was a little displeased with us, and they afflicted us more and more.
precepts.point: And no man shall buy you: no man shall redeem us from the curses. There is only one redeemer, brothers and sisters, and that is Christ.

note.label: Job Sees America's 250th Anniversary

precepts.why:
Moses said “thy life shall hang in doubt before thee”. When we got emancipated we thought we were free. Juneteenth. Then the white man took the sheet out of the closet, cut two holes in it, put on the white robe, and it was time for the KKK, patterned after the capirotes of Spain from the Inquisition. Spain was in this country, and what they had over there they brought here. As soon as we thought we were free, they gave us hell.

The Most High speaks to that in Zechariah: “And I am very sore displeased with the heathen that are at ease: for I was but a little displeased, and they helped forward the affliction.” God was a little displeased with us, because we broke his laws and his commandments. But the heathen afflicted us more and more and more. That is what God is saying right there.

Then back to Moses: “thou shalt fear day and night, and shalt have none assurance of thy life”. Imagine building your own town because white folks don't want you drinking their water or going to their school: your own cab company, your own hospital, your own bank. Then you hear a noise, and they are dropping dynamite on the city from planes and murdering a lot of us. That is the heathen helping forward the affliction, far beyond the little displeasure God had with us.

So the curses of Deuteronomy 28 came on us for our sins, but the nations went further than God sent them, and he is very sore displeased with them for it. The heathen that are at ease today are the ones who will answer for what they added to our affliction.

precepts.text: He sent to them by his messengers because he had compassion on his people, but they mocked the messengers and misused his prophets, until there was no remedy.
precepts.point: This is repetitive through the whole history. Any time the Most High sends a prophet to warn his people about destruction, that is compassion, because he did not have to do it.

note.label: Zechariah 1: Turn Ye Unto Me, and I Will Turn Unto You

precepts.why:
Be ye not as your fathers, unto whom the former prophets have cried. This is repetitive through the whole history. “And the Lord God of their fathers sent to them by his messengers, rising up betimes, and sending; because he had compassion on his people, and on his dwelling place”.

Any time the Most High sends a prophet to warn his people about destruction, that is compassion, because he did not have to do it. “But they mocked the messengers of God, and despised his words, and misused his prophets, until the wrath of the Lord arose against his people, till there was no remedy.” That is why he was sore displeased with our fathers: they did not hear, nor hearken, until there was no remedy. Turn ye unto me, and I will turn unto you, is that same compassion offered again.

precepts.text: Talk no more so exceeding proudly, for the Lord is a God of knowledge, and by him actions are weighed.
precepts.point: Talk is not what is weighed. Israel is judged by our doings.

note.label: Zechariah 1: Turn Ye Unto Me, and I Will Turn Unto You

precepts.why:
Our fathers returned and said, according to our ways and according to our doings, so hath he dealt with us. You get judged by the Most High based on your actions. “Talk no more so exceeding proudly; let not arrogancy come out of your mouth: for the Lord is a God of knowledge, and by him actions are weighed.”

Talk is not what is weighed. The Lord is a God of knowledge, and by him actions are weighed; Israel is judged by our doings.

points: And I am very sore displeased with the heathen that are at ease: for I was but a little displeased, and they helped forward the affliction. God was a little displeased, because we did sin, we did deserve to go into captivity. You can read Daniel chapter 9 if you disagree with it. God was righteous. He tried to call out to us by the prophets for thousands of years. He is righteous in all of his judgments.
And they helped forward the affliction. But the heathen did too much. He went beyond what was intended for us in serving in slavery. He did more than he was supposed to do to us.
